landing.title: Detect Early.
landing.subtitle: Protect Every Drop.
landing.description: AI-based predictive modelling for early forecasting of bovine mastitis. Combining simulated smart collar bio-metrics with in-line milk cup spectrometry.
landing.researchNotice: Precision Dairy Intelligence • Multi-sensor bovine telemetry and risk assessment
landing.storyHeading: Mastitis begins in silence, long before visible swelling.
landing.storyP1: Subclinical mastitis costs dairy operations millions annually in discarded yield and emergency treatments. By the time visual clots appear in milk, tissue inflammation is already established.
landing.storyP2: MastiCare AI demonstrates how continuous non-invasive telemetry—monitoring subtle deviations in body temperature, rumination rest cycles, and ionic conductivity—can forecast risk 36 to 72 hours before acute onset.
landing.collarMilkTelemetry: Synthetic collar & milk cup telemetry pipeline
landing.architectureSubtitle: Dual-stream IoT data feeds combined into a machine learning classification engine.
landing.collarDesc: Simulates continuous subcutaneous temperature and 3-axis accelerometer readings. Early systemic response triggers elevated thermal spikes and decreased rumination activity.
landing.milkDesc: Models automated milking cluster sensors measuring electrical conductivity (EC) and milk pH. Disrupted cell membranes cause sodium and chloride ion leakage into milk.
landing.engineDesc: Multi-class Random Forest & XGBoost classifier categorizing cows into Healthy, Moderate Risk, or High Risk, automatically dispatching triage alerts to the Veterinarian Portal.
landing.workflowTitle: From IoT Anomaly to Veterinary Action
landing.workflowDesc: Experience the full workflow: inject synthetic temperature spikes or ionic changes in the hardware simulator, watch the AI risk engine update instantly on the dashboard, and manage triage notes in the veterinary portal.
landing.heroDesc: AI-assisted mastitis risk forecasting through simulated animal-health telemetry and milk-quality indicators, designed to support timely veterinary intervention.
landing.demoNotice: Interactive Assessment Studio • Calibrated multi-sensor bovine health telemetry
landing.principlesDesc: Bovine mastitis produces subtle physiological alterations hours before visible inflammation or milk clots appear. Our system models four bio-physical telemetry streams to detect subclinical patterns early.
landing.tempDesc: Tracks systemic thermal elevation above 39.0°C. Bacterial infection triggers an internal pyretic reaction prior to gross tissue swelling.
landing.ruminationDesc: Measures collar-sensed neck movement and chewing frequency. Lethargy (<40 index) or reduced cud chewing flags visceral discomfort.
landing.ecDesc: Damaged mammary tight junctions leak Na+ and Cl- ions into milk. Conductivity surpassing 5.0 mS/cm is the gold-standard subclinical indicator.
landing.phDesc: Normal bovine milk is mildly acidic (6.50–6.80). Inflammation causes blood serum influx (pH 7.4), creating an alkaline shift toward >7.0.
landing.pipelineDesc: From simulated edge telemetry to veterinary case confirmation, every step is fully wired to our FastAPI backend and SQLite database.
landing.step1Desc: Choose a registered dairy cow with RFID, breed, and lactation history.
landing.step2Desc: Apply calibrated clinical presets or tune multi-sensor sliders.
landing.step3Desc: FastAPI executes Random Forest classifier across all four indicators.
landing.step4Desc: Displays 4-class risk category, softmax probabilities, and deviations.
landing.step5Desc: Elevated risk triggers automated alert creation with "New" status.
landing.step6Desc: Veterinarian reviews case, logs clinical notes, and updates alert status.
landing.testLoopBtn: Test This Complete Loop in Health Assessment
landing.presetsDesc: Our clinical assessment engine includes five pre-configured scenarios representing standard healthy states, subtle subclinical ionic drift, acute febrile mastitis, and isolated behavioral lethargy.
landing.riskResponseDesc: Clear separation between computational risk stratification and actionable clinical veterinary advice.
landing.noRiskAction: Continue standard milking hygiene and continuous autonomous telemetry polling.
landing.lowRiskDesc: Mild thermal rise (>39.2°C) or reduced rumination chewing without severe milk ionic change.
landing.lowRiskAction: Tag cow for prioritized sensor re-evaluation at subsequent milking session.
landing.modRiskDesc: Noticeable conductivity spike (>5.5 mS/cm) and alkaline pH shift indicating broken cellular barriers.
landing.modRiskAction: Perform California Mastitis Test (CMT), segregate milk, and inspect teat canal integrity.
landing.highRiskDesc: Multi-sensor critical markers: high fever (>40°C), acute lethargy, EC >6.5 mS/cm, pH >7.2.
landing.highRiskAction: Isolate quarter immediately. Automated emergency alert dispatched to attending veterinarian for physical exam.
landing.limitationsDesc: MastiCare AI is engineered with rigorous scientific validation and transparent reporting:
landing.limitation1Desc: Stratified across all four risk classes using published bovine veterinary ranges.
landing.limitation2Desc: Validated on an independent 20% holdout split (1,200 samples) with 10-fold cross validation (93.53% ± 0.65%).
landing.limitation3Desc: Telemetry models reflect physiological thresholds from veterinary literature, evaluated with calibrated synthetic data streams.
landing.limitation4Desc: Software risk forecasts are assistive alerts designed for prompt triage and do not constitute a licensed clinical diagnosis.

detail.riskHighDesc: Subcutaneous temperature exceeds 39.5°C with electrical conductivity above 5.5 mS/cm. This pattern reflects tight-junction breakdown between mammary secretory cells and sodium/chloride leakage into milk. High probability of acute or severe subclinical mastitis.
detail.riskHighAction: Recommended Veterinary Action: Isolate milking unit, perform CMT quarter test, and evaluate somatic cell count (SCC).
detail.riskModDesc: Temperature is slightly elevated (>39.0°C) or milk electrical conductivity is beginning to diverge (>5.0 mS/cm). Early inflammatory response or transient physiological stress.
detail.riskModAction: Recommended Veterinary Action: Flag cow for continuous telemetry observation; re-check conductivity over next 2 milking cycles.
detail.riskStableDesc: All telemetry streams remain within healthy reference baselines. Core body temperature is between 38.0–39.0°C, activity index is normal, and milk electrical conductivity is below 5.0 mS/cm with normal milk pH.
detail.riskStableAction: Standard Protocol: Continue routine herd monitoring.
